title: antitrust / divestiture / merger remedies | Research Paper | Antitrust on Aisle Five: How Well Do Divestiture Remedies Wo...
summary: This paper examines the long-run effectiveness of structural divestiture remedies used by antitrust authorities in merger cases. Using census-level establishment data and proprietary transaction records from the U.S. grocery sector, the authors find that divested stores experience an average 31 percent decline in employment over five years, driven by elevated exit rates and persistent contraction. The authors conclude that structural remedies may be less effective when merging parties retain substantial discretion over which assets are divested and to which buyers.
